subject: Post-demo tech recap: vector dims, batching & auth for DeepDive POC
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thomas <claire.thomas@deepdive.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@deepdive.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-17T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo tech recap: vector dims, batching & auth for DeepDive POC

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the clear outline of your recommender goals.  Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps for the POC so we can validate latency and unit-cost for your product recommender use case.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Query traffic: ~120 req/s during peak for product pages (90% single-utterance queries).
- Candidates per query: 250–1,000 depending on feed.
- Current provider: you mentioned a hosted vector DB plus a custom reranker that scores top-200.

Technical recommendations to validate in the POC:
1) Vector dimensionality
   - Start with 512d to match your current model embeddings; we can test 256d later if cost/latency tradeoffs look favorable.
2) Batching & concurrency
   - Use continuous batching with target micro-batch size 16 for encoder-side inference and 64 for embedding ingestion. This keeps tail latency in 50–120ms ballpark on our Dedicated nodes.
3) Normalization
   - L2-normalize embeddings before storage; Redwood can accept pre-normalized vectors or apply an options flag at write-time.
4) Migration from your provider
   - We can stream a delta import from your existing vector DB (incremental reindex) and run side-by-side sampling for quality checks.
5) Auth & SDK setup
   - Recommended: service-account token + short-lived client tokens for frontend calls. We'll provide a short sample that uses our SDK and a server-side proxy pattern for auth.
6) Routing & fault-tolerance
   - Region-aware routing: route queries to us-west primary; fallback to us-east reserved capacity if latency crosses threshold.

Attachments: architecture-diagram.png (POC topology), sample-embed-calls.txt (SDK snippets + curl).

Next steps I propose:
- Technical sync (30 min) next Tue — deep dive on ingestion pipeline and reranker inputs.
- Redwood to provide baseline perf numbers with 512d and 256d test payloads (we'll run small sampling job).
- You to share a sanitized sample of 50k candidate vectors and a sample scoring function (or reranker example).

If that all looks good I can loop in our solutions engineer (Marissa) to scope the ingest job and set up temporary Dedicated lanes for the POC.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0128

Date: 2027-01-18T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo tech recap: vector dims, batching & auth for DeepDive POC

Thanks Ava — this is super helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying notes from our side: 

- We currently store 768d vectors (legacy model). We're open to re-embedding to 512d but want to measure retrieval/regression risk.
- Peak candidate set per query after filtering is ~600; reranker takes top-200.
- We run ingestion jobs nightly; incremental near-real-time updates are desirable for hot items.

Would love to do the tech sync Tuesday 11am PT. I'll attach a sanitized dump of 10k vectors and our scoring pseudo-code in a follow-up (don't need full dataset yet).

Can Marissa be on the call to scope the ingest job and confirm stateful reranker options?

Thanks,
Claire
Head of ML Engineering, DeepDive Retail
claire.thomas@deepdive.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thomas <claire.thomas@deepdive.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T11:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo tech recap: vector dims, batching & auth for DeepDive POC

Adding a few notes from SE perspective ahead of Tuesday:

1) Migration approach
- We recommend a two-pass migration: (A) bulk import to a staging index, (B) run verification sampling (nDCG/recall on golden queries) before cutover. This minimizes risk compared to direct overwrite.

2) Performance plan
- For 600 candidate sets + top-200 reranker: plan to run dense retrieval on a shard set with query-time batching of 8–16. Reranker (re-scoring) can be colocated on CPU or small GPU depending on model size.

3) Normalization & storage
- If you choose 512d, we can provide an on-write L2-normalization hook in the ingest pipeline. We also suggest storing raw + normalized vectors (adds ~2x storage for retraining traces but helps ablation).

4) SDK/auth snippets (attached)
- sample-embed-calls.txt includes: server-side token exchange + Python SDK ingest example and a best-practice pattern for short-lived tokens for the browser.

5) Observability
- We'll enable per-route latency and token-cost dashboards for the POC and a small evaluation set to detect model-quality regressions (prompted ranking mismatches).

Prep for the call: please share:
- sanitized 10k vector sample (Claire said you will)
- example reranker model/spec (input features + sample scoring)
- a prioritized set of 30 golden queries we can use for nDCG checks

I'll run a quick import on staging once we have the sample and share perf numbers (tail p95/p99, avg ingest throughput).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: sample-embed-calls.txt
